entries.definition: The technical-literature process by which a generative model trained iteratively on its own (or its predecessors') outputs suffers a measurable degeneration of its output distribution — narrowed tail coverage, amplified mode bias — across successive training generations.
entries.scope_note: Local operationalization for this profile only; not a claim about every use of the phrase in the wider literature. Applied here (task-packets/K1-T04.yaml) to the three theory-atlas papers matching a fixed, disclosed keyword search ("model collapse", "model-collapse", "self-consuming", "self-consumption", "autophagy", "MAD", "curse of recursion") over tags/summary/work: shumailov-curse-of-recursion, alemohammad-self-consuming-generative-models-go-mad, gerstgrasser-is-model-collapse-inevitable.

entries.definition: A work 'instantiates' the mechanism when its own production pipeline demonstrably trains on model-generated outputs across at least two generations; a work merely 'references' the mechanism when it only discusses, depicts, or alludes to it without demonstrable recursive training. Decision procedure, applied directly against each work's own `decisive_move` + `source_url` field in the pinned works-atlas snapshot: Step 1 -- does the work's own documented production process feed model-GENERATED output back in as training input for a SUBSEQUENT generation of the same (or a continuous) generative pipeline, across at least two generations? If yes -> instantiates. Step 2 -- if the work only depicts, critiques, or thematizes the phenomenon, or trains on human-authored material (even the artist's own prior writing) without a demonstrable model-generation-to-model-generation loop -> references only. Ambiguous or incompletely disclosed cases -> qualifies, assessed individually, never force-fit into either bucket.
entries.scope_note: Applied here (task-packets/K1-T04.yaml) to the 15 works-atlas entries whose own `clusters` array contains 7 ("AI self-consumption"); each classification's basis is recorded in corpora/model-collapse/corpus-entries.json's own `extraction.classification_basis` field, quoting the exact `decisive_move` text it rests on.
